text: Ah, the humble candle. A magnificent vessel of hope, crafted primarily from the refined essence of dead dinosaurs and ancient forests, now distilled into a sticky, flammable sludge that we pay a premium to burn in our dimly lit apartments. It is the ultimate symbol of adult sophistication: a stick of wax that costs more per ounce than gold, designed to emit a faint, flickering glow while slowly consuming the very air you are trying to breathe. It is not merely a light source; it is a testament to our collective delusion that we can create "ambiance" while simultaneously ignoring the fact that we are essentially lighting a fuse to our own financial stability. The wax drips down the side like tears of joy for a job well done, or perhaps just like the sweat of anxiety as you wonder if you left the stove on. It is, quite literally, a burning investment.
